items.title: Flat pullback of the divisor of a rational function is the sum of the divisors on the irreducible components of the source
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the flat pullback of the divisor of a rational function on an integral base of dimension k: it is the sum over the irreducible components X_j of the source of the multiplicity of X_j times the divisor of the pulled back function on X_j (statement lines 3097-3110, tag 0EPH). The proof compares coefficients after reducing to the case where the image of the chosen cycle is a prime divisor, then translates the two coefficients into lengths over a flat local map A -> B and reduces the whole statement to one length identity involving length_A(A/(x)) and length_B(B/xB), which is finished by additivity over the minimal primes of B. The translation into the local length identity is the substance, so the claim is H2.
